newsitem.title: TOGO: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICA BACK IN WORLD CUP HUNT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICA BACK IN WORLD CUP HUNT.

text.p: Phil Masinga and Doctor Khumalo returned to national colours on Sunday and scored a goal each as South Africa revitalised their World Cup hopes with a 2-1 (half-time 1-1) qualifying group win over Zaire.

Midfielder Khumalo, restored to the side after sitting out the last two matches, scored first and Masinga, playing his first game since ending a short self-imposed retirement from international soccer, got the winner in a tense match played in neutral Togo because of the civil war conflict in Zaire.
The result put South Africa back on top of the group, level with Congo, who were beaten 3-0 by Zambia in Lusaka earlier in the day.
South Africa had a shot cleared off the line after just 50 seconds and a goal disallowed in the second minute before Khumalo curled in the opening goal in the 21st minute.
But a slip by new captain Lucas Radebe allowed Zaire an equaliser just four minutes later through burly 19-year-old striker Zico Tumbu.

Tumbu, who turns 20 on Tuesday and is a reserve team player at French club F.C.Metz, was making his debut and following in the footsteps of his father, who played in the 1974 World Cup finals in Germany.

Khumalo hit the crossbar soon after and South African midfielder John Moshoeu also struck the woodwork before former Leeds United striker Masinga powered in the winner with his header in the 71st minute.
Masinga missed South Africa's last qualifier against Congo three weeks ago after abuse from home fans prompted him to quit international football.
Zaire might have equalised with the final shot of the match but Ndombasi Landou's effort hit the upright and bounced away.

Zaire: 16-Botende Eshele; 18-Okita Nkoy Kimoto, 17-Michel Dinzey, 4-Ndama Bapupa, 15-Epangala Lokose; 12-Ekanza Simba (6-Epotele Bazamba 57th minute), 8-Ndombasi Landou, 14-Ngoy Nsumbu, 7-Emeka Mamale, 11-Etienne Nsunda; 9-Zico Tumbu (13-Kiala Muzinga 51st)

South Africa: 1-Andre Arendse; 2-Sizwe Motaung, 5-Mark Fish, 19-Lucas Radebe, 3-David Nyathi; 21-Eric Tinkler, 22-Dumisa Ngobe (11-Helman Mkhalele 67th), 15-Doctor Khumalo (18-John Moeti 75th), 10-John Moshoeu; 6-Phil Masinga (17-Shaun Bartlett 79th),12-Brendan Augustine
